title: Post-Mortem: Why a 14-Month Manufacturing ERP Project Failed (And How We Rescued It in 60 Days)
content:
In early 2026, we were approached by the board of an industrial plastics manufacturing plant in Egypt. They had spent 14 months and over $75,000 with an international agency attempting an ERP implementation.

Yet on the production floor, workers still tracked resin consumption on whiteboards.

Here is our frank post-mortem of why that project collapsed:

1. Scope Bloat Before Adoption: The previous agency tried to model complex multi-level robotic work center scheduling on day one. When operators struggled to log in, the whole schedule stopped.
2. Neglected Floor Realities: Technicians on the factory floor wore industrial gloves and couldn't operate standard tiny web buttons on a touchscreen.
3. Disconnected Scrap Tracking: Raw material shrinkage wasn't accounted for at the machine level, skewing the general ledger.

How Scando Led the 60-Day Rescue:
- Phase 1 (Days 1–20): We stripped out 42 custom modules and restored standard Odoo Manufacturing (MRP) with large-button industrial kiosk screens.
- Phase 2 (Days 21–40): Automated raw material issue slips directly tied to machine lot numbers via simple barcode scans.
- Phase 3 (Days 41–60): Live finished goods reconciliation tying directly to warehouse pallet storage.

Result: 100% shop floor logging compliance within 3 weeks, and the plant closed its first accurate monthly production cost balance in 2 years.

Rescue projects aren't about writing more code. They are about cutting the excess and respecting frontline human behavior.
